claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the basics:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I have one child I'd like to check eligibility for - my son Alex, he's 9 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm assessing eligibility for your son, Alex, who is 9 years old.

Before I can make a determination, I need to understand more about your situation. Let me start with an important question:

**Do you live with Alex, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me - he lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex lives with his mum rather than with you, I need to understand the situation a bit more.

**Are you the father of Alex, and are you providing financial support for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his dad, and I do help out financially - I contribute towards his needs regularly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I understand you're Alex's father and you do provide financial support to him.

To properly assess your eligibility, I need to check the specific rules about Child Benefit when a child lives with someone else. Let me review the relevant guidance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, I've reviewed the guidance. Based on what you've told me, here's what's important:

The rules state that you can continue to get Child Benefit for more than 8 weeks if you contribute to your child's upkeep by an amount **equal to or more than the Child Benefit payment itself**. This includes contributions towards clothes, food, pocket money, and financial contributions towards their accommodation.

I have one more important question:

**How much are you currently contributing towards Alex's upkeep each week or month, and are you aware of what the current Child Benefit payment rate is?** (The current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for the first child, but please tell me what you're contributing so I can assess this properly.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £30 a week towards Alex's needs - things like clothes, school stuff, and helping out with what he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's very helpful.

Based on what you've told me and the guidance I've reviewed, let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex:

**Your situation:**
- Alex is 9 years old (eligible age - under 16)
- Alex lives with his mum (not with you)
- You contribute approximately £30 per week towards his upkeep (clothes, school stuff, and his needs)
- The current Child Benefit payment rate is £25.60 per week for the first child

**Why you are eligible:**

According to the rules, when a child lives with someone else, you can continue to receive Child Benefit if you contribute to the child's upkeep by an amount equal to or more than the Child Benefit payment itself. Your contribution of £30 per week exceeds the Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week, which means you meet this requirement.

The regulations specifically state that upkeep includes clothes, presents, food, and pocket money - all of which you're contributing towards.

Let me now provide your formal eligibility determination:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Congratulations!** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

To proceed with your claim, you'll need to contact the Child Benefit Office. Make sure to have evidence of your regular contributions towards Alex's upkeep ready, as you may be asked to provide documentation showing your financial support.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your eligibility?
